newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Gold - Indian sub-continent prices seen falling.

text.p: A downtrend in world gold markets is expected to keep prices in the Indian sub-continent subdued in the next few days, dealers and analysts said on Monday.
Dealers said prospects of cheaper gold imports triggered speculative selling, pushing prices down by 50 rupees to 5,090 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Monday.
"Wedding season buying remained poor and lower than expected while higher arrivals and unloading by stockists undermined market sentiment," said Babubhai Jain, a top jeweller.
"Sliding global prices have reduced the cost of imported gold which in turn, has affected prices in the local market," Jain said. "I expect a further fall in the next few days."
Dealers said they would expect imports of gold to pick up following lower prices in international markets and margins that importers would have on sales in India.

Market sentiment turned weak following an assurance in New Delhi by the commerce secretary last week that the government was considering allowing higher imports of gold against special licences and also reducing import duty on gold.
Expatriate Indians are allowed to bring in up to five kgs of gold once every six months subject to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes.
In Pakistan's commercial city of Karachi, gold prices are likely to ease in the week beginning Monday in line with the trend in international markets, dealers said.
In Dubai, gold traders on Sunday pinned hopes on the Indian wedding season and an improved harvest to rejuvenate a subdued market by the end of the year.
"Demand is not so good because the market in India is slow and most of our sales here depend on the market there," said a Dubai souk (market) trader.
"But we hope it will pick up on more demand, including the wedding season, as the year ends," the trader said.
The second Indian marriage season, which begins around mid-November and concludes by February-end, usually sees a strong upturn in bullion and jewellery purchases.
Much of Indian purchases are met by supplies from Dubai where prices are lower than in Bombay.
Gold prices, 24 carats per 10 grammes, in U.S. dollars -
(Conversion 1$=35.70 Indian rupees, 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices December 2 & November 26, Karachi and Dubai prices December 1 & November 25 respectively. --Dev Varam, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
